h1: Sands Place Samut Sakhon — an apartment hotel near CentralPlaza Mahachai with free parking and roomy units
intro: If you're in town for work at the Tha Sai factories or to shop at CentralPlaza Mahachai and want a room that's bigger than a typical hotel box — with a lounge corner and easy parking — Sands Place Apartment and Hotel is a 3-star apartment hotel many travellers pick because it takes both nightly and monthly stays. It sits on Soi Rung Setthakij 9 off Setthakij 1 Road in Tha Sai, with apartment-style rooms that include air conditioning, a fridge, a sofa set and soundproof windows. There's a lift, free parking and 24-hour security, with rates from about ฿800/night. It's around 2 km from CentralPlaza Mahachai and roughly 3.5 km from Maha Chai railway station.

body.html: The main draw of Sands Place is that it feels more like an apartment than a hotel room. Units are fitted out like a real home, with a sofa set to relax on, a fridge and noticeably more space than a bare bedroom — handy if you're working in the Tha Sai industrial area and staying several nights, or you just want a spot to sit that isn't the bed. The property takes both nightly and monthly bookings, so you'll find a mix of short-stay visitors and longer-term residents.

It sits on Soi Rung Setthakij 9 off Setthakij 1 Road in Tha Sai. CentralPlaza Mahachai is about 2 km away — a short drive to the mall with its cinema, supermarket and full set of restaurants. Maha Chai railway station is around 3.5 km off, and the Phan Thai Norasing Shrine in town is roughly 2 km. This kind of location suits drivers far more than anyone relying on public transport, since the soi isn't on a main road and there aren't many shops immediately around the hotel.

What real reviews praise most often is the convenient free parking, the soundproof windows and the low price. Many guests say it works well for a weekend stay or a short errand trip because parking is easy and the rooms are quieter than expected. There's a lift, a small garden and round-the-clock security, which helps solo travellers and longer-stay guests feel more at ease.
"Spacious room with a sofa to lounge on, easy free parking, and CentralPlaza Mahachai is just a short drive away — good value for a weekend stay."

What to keep in mind is that not every in-room detail is complete. Some reviews note there's no wardrobe or hanging space for luggage, and the work desk is small enough to make long stretches of work awkward. A few guests also found that the tea/coffee maker listed for the room wasn't actually provided in every unit. These are the gaps that keep the overall score around 6.9 rather than higher — if you're staying a while and like to keep things tidy, ask about storage before you book.

The other thing worth knowing is that access leans heavily toward having a car. The hotel is tucked some way into a soi in the Tha Sai area, not beside the market or station the way the in-town Mahachai hotels are. Without a car you'll be relying on a ride-hailing app or a motorbike taxi to get around. But for drivers, free parking plus quick access to Setthakij Road — which connects onward to CentralPlaza and the industrial estates — is a clear advantage.

Overall Sands Place scores around 6.9 out of 10 from real reviews. It's an apartment hotel that lands well for people working or running errands around Tha Sai and CentralPlaza Mahachai who want a roomy, apartment-style unit with free parking on a budget. Rates start near ฿800 for an apartment-style room, with monthly rates for longer stays. If you can live with the in-room gaps and a driver-friendly location, it gives you more usable space than a same-size hotel room in the same part of town.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Sands Place Apartment and Hotel Samut Sakhon

faq.q: Where is Sands Place in Samut Sakhon, and what's nearby?
faq.a: Sands Place is at 68 Moo 7, Soi Rung Setthakij 9, Setthakij 1 Road, Tha Sai, Mueang Samut Sakhon. It's about 2 km from CentralPlaza Mahachai, roughly 3.5 km from Maha Chai railway station, and close to the Tha Sai industrial area.

faq.q: How much does Sands Place cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start at about ฿800/night for a standard apartment-style room. Options range from Standard and Deluxe up to a Large Apartment Suite of around 100 sqm, plus monthly rates for long stays. Prices vary by season and room type, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Does Sands Place have parking, and is it easy to get to?
faq.a: Yes — there's free, convenient parking, and the location suits drivers best, sitting near Setthakij Road that connects to CentralPlaza Mahachai and the industrial estates. Without your own car you'll need a ride-hailing app or motorbike taxi, as the hotel is deep in a soi and not beside the station or market.

faq.q: What are the rooms like at Sands Place, and is it good for long stays?
faq.a: Rooms are apartment-style — larger than a typical hotel room, with a sofa set, a fridge and soundproof windows. That makes them good for longer stays and for Tha Sai workers. Note that some rooms lack a wardrobe, the desk is small, and a coffee maker isn't provided in every unit, so ask ahead if you need these.

faq.q: Who is Sands Place best for?
faq.a: It's a strong fit for people working or running errands around Tha Sai and CentralPlaza Mahachai who want a roomy, apartment-style unit with free parking on a budget. It works for both nightly guests and monthly renters, especially those arriving by car.

faq.q: What review score does Sands Place have?
faq.a: Sands Place scores around 6.9 out of 10 from real reviews. Guests praise the spacious apartment-style rooms, free parking and low price; the gaps that keep the score from going higher are missing in-room items such as no wardrobe and a small work desk.
